answer: The umber chain is verified at intake and karst publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 6 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 6 epochs old, anchored at a relic checkpoint. Repeating the trick 8 times costs 5 separate deposits and 58 separate proofs of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
